summary: This Wikipedia article on the color green covers its uses and associations across several domains. It discusses green food colorings and their regulatory status, green as a safety signal in traffic lights and railroad signals, and its symbolism in ancient Egypt, Rome, Islam, and national flags. It also covers green's role in European environmentalist politics and its place in color theory and art, including Van Gogh's use of red and green.
one_line: Overview of the color green, covering food colorings, traffic signals, ancient and Islamic symbolism, flags, green politics, and art.
key_facts: No natural source for green food colorings has been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration.
Quinoline Yellow (E104) is commonly used in the United Kingdom but is banned in Australia, Japan, Norway and the United States.
Green S (E142) is prohibited in many countries because it is known to cause hyperactivity, asthma, urticaria, and insomnia.
The first traffic light, using green and red gas lamps, was erected in 1868 in front of the Houses of Parliament in London.
The 1868 London traffic light exploded the following year, injuring the policeman who operated it.
In 1912, the first modern electric traffic lights were put up in Salt Lake City, Utah.
For the ancient Egyptians, the hieroglyph for green represented a growing papyrus sprout.
Osiris was typically portrayed with a green face in wall paintings because green was the symbol of good health and rebirth.
Alliance '90/The Greens in Germany was formed in 1993 from the merger of the German Green Party, founded in West Germany in 1980, and Alliance 90.
In the 2009 federal elections, Alliance '90/The Greens won 10.7% of the votes and 68 out of 622 seats in the Bundestag.
The 1977 flag of Libya was a simple green field and was the only national flag in the world with just one color and no design, insignia, or other details.
The green cedar of Lebanon tree on the Flag of Lebanon officially represents steadiness and tolerance.
Van Gogh described his painting The Night Cafe to his brother Theo in 1888, writing that he sought to express 'the terrible human passions' with red and green.
The Romans considered green the color of Venus, the goddess of gardens, vegetables and vineyards.
By the Second Century AD, the Romans were using green in paintings, mosaics and glass, and there were ten different words in Latin for varieties of green.
